story.title: Little Pip's Big Change
story.text:
SC01_ST01_N = Look at the green leaf.
SC01_ST02_N = There is a small egg.
SC01_ST03_N = It shakes a little.
SC02_ST01_N = Crack!
SC02_ST02_N = Crack!
SC02_ST03_N = A small caterpillar comes out.
SC02_ST04_N = His name is Pip.
SC03_ST01_N = Pip is very hungry.
SC03_ST02_N = He takes a big chomp.
SC03_ST03_N = Chomp, chomp, chomp!
SC04_ST01_N = Pip eats all day long.
SC04_ST02_N = Soon, the leaf has many holes.
SC05_ST01_N = Then Pip hears a little voice.
SC05_ST02_N = "Hello?" says the voice.
SC05_ST03_N = Pip looks through a hole.
SC06_ST01_N = There is another caterpillar!
SC06_ST02_N = "Hi!"
SC06_ST03_N = I'm Dot," she says.
SC06_ST04_N = They become friends.
SC07_ST01_N = Pip and Dot eat together.
SC07_ST02_N = Chomp, chomp, chomp!
SC07_ST03_N = Pip grows and grows.
SC08_ST01_N = "This is fun!"
SC08_ST02_N = Pip says.
SC08_ST03_N = But Pip's eyes slowly close.
SC08_ST04_N = He feels very sleepy.
SC09_ST01_N = Dot smiles kindly.
SC09_ST02_N = "Goodbye for now, Pip," she says.
SC09_ST03_N = "See you soon!"
SC10_ST01_N = Pip makes a hard little house.
SC10_ST02_N = It is dark inside.
SC10_ST03_N = Pip sleeps for a long time.
SC11_ST01_N = One sunny morning, the hard house cracks.
SC11_ST02_N = Crack!
SC11_ST03_N = Crack!
SC11_ST04_N = Something comes out slowly.
SC12_ST01_N = Dot comes to the house.
SC12_ST02_N = "Pip?" she whispers.
SC12_ST03_N = "Is that you?"
SC13_ST01_N = Pip has bright orange wings now.
SC13_ST02_N = He flaps them slowly.
SC13_ST03_N = "I can fly!" he says.
SC14_ST01_N = Pip flies above the flowers.
SC14_ST02_N = Dot waves from the leaf.
SC14_ST03_N = "You are beautiful, Pip!"
SC15_ST01_N = Pip lands beside Dot.
SC15_ST02_N = "I will wait for you now," he says.
SC15_ST03_N = Then they smile at each other.

sentences.text: Soon, the leaf has many holes.
Then Pip hears a little voice.
Pip makes a hard little house.
Pip sleeps for a long time.
One sunny morning, the hard house cracks.
Pip has bright orange wings now.
"I will wait for you now," he says.
Then they smile at each other.

questions.instruction: Look at the picture. Choose one answer at a time.
questions.hint: Start with Who. Then choose What and Where.

assessmentMetadata.operationalSkill: Identify who, what, and where with reduced choice load

responseRubric.definitionKo: 문항이 요구하는 핵심 Story Element와 관계를 정확히 이해한 증거가 있습니다.
responseRubric.studentFeedbackKo: 이야기가 시작될 때 누가, 어디에서, 어떤 상황에 있었는지 모두 정확히 찾았어요.

responseRubric.recommendedActionKo: 첫 장면의 인물·장소·처음 상황을 한 문장으로 설명합니다.
responseRubric.studentFeedbackEn: You found who, where, and what happened first!

responseRubric.definitionKo: 핵심 정보는 파악했지만 순서·관계·세부 단서의 일부가 불완전합니다.

responseRubric.parentFeedbackKo: 세 가지 배경 요소 중 대부분을 정확히 파악했으나 한 요소에서 후속 장면과의 혼동이 나타납니다. 다음 활동: 틀린 한 요소를 첫 장면에서 다시 찾아 표시합니다.

responseRubric.studentFeedbackEn: You found most of the story clues. Check one box again.

responseRubric.definitionKo: 이야기의 관련 요소는 인식했지만 질문이 요구하는 핵심 관계를 잘못 연결했습니다.
responseRubric.studentFeedbackKo: 인물·장소·처음 상황 중 한 가지는 찾았어요. 나머지 요소도 첫 장면에서 다시 찾아보세요.
responseRubric.parentFeedbackKo: 배경의 일부 요소는 인식하지만 처음 장면과 이후 사건의 인물·장소·상황을 혼동합니다. 다음 활동: Who / Where / At first를 색으로 나누어 Story Map에 적습니다.
responseRubric.recommendedActionKo: Who / Where / At first를 색으로 나누어 Story Map에 적습니다.
responseRubric.studentFeedbackEn: You found one story clue. Check where it belongs.

responseRubric.definitionKo: 응답하지 않았거나 문항의 핵심 이해를 뒷받침하는 증거가 없습니다.
responseRubric.studentFeedbackKo: 첫 장면을 다시 보고 ‘누가, 어디에서, 처음에 무엇을 했는지’를 함께 찾아봐요.
responseRubric.parentFeedbackKo: 현재 응답에서는 이야기의 초기 배경 요소를 구분한 증거가 확인되지 않습니다. 다음 활동: 첫 장면을 다시 보고 인물부터 함께 찾은 뒤 장소와 상황으로 확장합니다.
responseRubric.recommendedActionKo: 첫 장면을 다시 보고 인물부터 함께 찾은 뒤 장소와 상황으로 확장합니다.
responseRubric.studentFeedbackEn: Look at the picture again. Start with “Who?”

assessmentFramework.name: Core Story Comprehension Check
assessmentFramework.theoreticalBasis: Story Grammar-informed; operationalized for a four-question, story-specific comprehension check.
assessmentFramework.interpretationBoundary: Results describe evidence from this story and these four tasks; they are not a Story Grammar proficiency score.
assessmentFramework.q1Design: Who, What, and Where are revealed one at a time. Each step presents only two same-category options.

reporting.overallFormula: Internal summary only: average the four ordered question scores.
reporting.profileRule: Use the response pattern and lowest story area to select feedback; do not interpret the average as Story Grammar proficiency.
